    <item>
      <title>Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya</link>
      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba</link>
      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/24/social-media-big-tech-fines-global-revenue-australia-digital-duty-care-laws</link>
      <description><p>Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech firms for harm suffered online under compromise deal </p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/24/labor-penny-wong-us-china-anthony-albanese-final-sitting-week-ntwnfb">Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Big tech companies may face “multibillion-dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court under <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/28/emotional-intimacy-ai-chatbots-ban-digital-duty-of-care-laws-australian-politics">Australia’s new digital duty of care</a> laws, with the Greens to support the bill’s passage after extracting major amendments from Labor.</p><p>From late 2027, Australians will also be able opt out of addictive online algorithms under the new legislation, while <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/09/labor-australians-opt-out-online-algorithms-how-change-feed#:~:text=A%20few%20features%20will%20be%20classified%20as%20having%20%E2%80%9Cnegative%20behavioural%20impacts%E2%80%9D%3A%20endless%20scroll">the “endless scroll” of social media feeds</a> may also cease.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/24/social-media-big-tech-fines-global-revenue-australia-digital-duty-care-laws">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/australian-politics">Australian politics</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/technology">Technology</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/meta">Meta</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/australia-news">Australia news</category>
      <pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:47:59 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/24/social-media-big-tech-fines-global-revenue-australia-digital-duty-care-laws</guid>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/24/labor-penny-wong-us-china-anthony-albanese-final-sitting-week-ntwnfb</link>

But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.</p><p>You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:35:19 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>France to establish 'strategic stockpiles' of critical minerals</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261124-france-to-establish-strategic-stockpiles-of-critical-minerals</link><description>
France will build up "strategic stocks" of "rare earths and certain priority metals", inspired by the reserves that exist for oil, in order to offset the dependence of industries, particularly on China, the presidency said on Monday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bd2bb056-47a9-11f0-849e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-06-06T233428Z-1190243769-RC2CXEAF7E6N-RTRMADP-3-USA-CHINA-MINERALS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bd2bb056-47a9-11f0-849e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-06-06T233428Z-1190243769-RC2CXEAF7E6N-RTRMADP-3-USA-CHINA-MINERALS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4325fb4-e7df-11f1-b823-2f2b2f37c80f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:10:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bd2bb056-47a9-11f0-849e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-06-06T233428Z-1190243769-RC2CXEAF7E6N-RTRMADP-3-USA-CHINA-MINERALS.jpg">REUTERS - David Becker</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron pledges €350m for aviation research, pushes industrial acceleration</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-macron-pledges-%E2%82%AC350m-for-aviation-research-pushes-industrial-acceleration-choose-france-investment</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research, and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its reindustrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a2ef3750-e74c-11f1-a595-b587b1fd65db</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 15:46:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/28be4364-e74b-11f1-adb6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-23T113419Z-993058008-RC2NTOAX1REF-RTRMADP-3-AIRBUS-FRANCE.jpg">© Manon Cruz/Pool via Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261123-major-cyberattack-hits-it-systems-at-guadeloupe-university-hospital</link><description>
A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postponing non-emergency procedures.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">dee6caee-e728-11f1-80df-9f0d9c8f7db3</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:45:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0516acf0-2372-11ec-81e8-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_9M94VC.jpg">© Carla Bernhardt/AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec3acb0c-e4dd-11f1-9619-3935a39ed096</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:24:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5f6cabe8-e1a7-11f1-8f6a-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/gerry.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-france-probes-suspected-leaks-from-interior-ministry-to-far-right-national-rally</link><description>
France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5be0a25a-e4b2-11f1-be46-714476ef8919</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:55:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0777260e-e45c-11f1-a6ff-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/000-9QL2XA.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French union leader warns strikes will continue without higher wages</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-union-leader-warns-strikes-will-continue-without-higher-wages-cgt-sophie-binet-interview</link><description>
French trade unions have promised to call more strikes and demonstrations, arguing that a government proposal to increase the minimum wage fails to address the social crisis that has spurred protests across the country. Sophie Binet, head of the CGT union, says even after six weeks of action, workers and students are more determined than ever to keep up the fight.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37c8b342-e40f-11f1-a821-bd0c1d2fd9c6</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 06:07:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/60fce194-d932-11f1-aa3d-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T160039Z-986160219-RC2PHOAZFNU3-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© REUTERS - Sarah Meyssonnier </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da07160a-e41c-11f1-9424-dd481487d627</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:19:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261119-france-raises-bird-flu-alert-to-highest-level-as-infections-spread-across-europe</link><description>
France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eff2afda-e3f7-11f1-a0c0-bdb47d3d53b3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:12:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png">© GAIZKA IROZ / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. Although turnout was lower than at previous protests, anger remained strong – with many demonstrators also voicing fears about the far right coming to power in the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b33b0b8-e32a-11f1-9717-657339b41114</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:50:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5222ba24-e2a9-11f1-8d87-7908c4e1a3c7/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T145907Z-1351244212-RC2QPOAW8GVH-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Gonzalo Fuentes</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>EU economics chief warns France and Belgium must reduce deficit and public debt</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-eu-economics-chief-warns-france-and-belgium-must-reduce-deficit-and-public-debt</link><description>
France and Belgium must bring down their public debt and deficit levels, European Union economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis warned on Tuesday as he unveiled the European Commission's autumn economic forecast. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">065f0570-e281-11f1-84fb-2734eec1674a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:00:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/10c6be26-e291-11f1-a882-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-17T111747Z-863268942-RC2MPOA5EG14-RTRMADP-3-BELGIUM-PROTEST-STUDENTS.jpg">REUTERS - Yves Herman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'A message to drug gangs': life sentences for 'barbaric' Marseille murders</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-a-message-to-drug-gangs-life-sentences-for-barbaric-marseille-murders</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1288fd3c-e282-11f1-91a0-f16e280f34ca</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:59:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/643239e4-e1ee-11f1-a552-5f54d898a954/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D3QA9QV.jpg">AFP - THIBAUD MORITZ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French presidential candidates clash over tax, housing and the minimum wage</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261117-french-presidential-candidates-clash-over-tax-housing-and-the-minimum-wage</link><description>

      <description><p>Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/nov/23/nvidia-board-jensen-huang-return">Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline">Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang</a></p></li></ul><p>Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">the tech billionaire’s downfall</a>.</p><p>Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC.       <title>Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/jensen-huang-nvidia-john-kennedy</link>
      <description><p>John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips</p><p>Invoking Greek mythology, the US senator John Kennedy has characterized former <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a> chief executive officer <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the <a href="https://x.com/atrupar/status/2124514031209980207?a=ArDF3m1PBQGZjNDPrME&amp;s=20">most expensive</a> sex since Helen of Troy”.</p><p>The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/jensen-huang-testify-congress-nvidia-affair-spy">put at risk</a> by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/jensen-huang-nvidia-john-kennedy">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Carry cash and know your rights: how to fly in the US this Thanksgiving holiday</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer</link>
      <description><p>Amid air chaos, travelers will have to navigate an outdated system (and complex company policies if it all goes wrong)</p><p>Millions of people are planning to fly in the US over the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the US Federal Aviation Administration’s 13 November <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11 (aside from a brief halt in 2023).</p><p>In the chaos that ensued, some travelers embarked on <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/royalcaribbean/comments/1xvkopq/comment/19smxjywidlcw/?context=3">overnight drives</a> to catch cruise ships and <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/women-stranded-faa-ground-stop-buy-ford-bronco-27-hour-road-trip-rcna609629">bought new cars</a> to make business meetings. Many had to simply cancel their plans and incur the costs that came with it. More than 18,000 flights were cancelled at a potential cost to travelers of $1.9bn in lost time and related expenses, <a href="https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/analysis-nationwide-ground-stop-cost-travelers-nearly-2-billion/">Anderson Economic Group estimates</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league</link>
      <description><p>Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club</p><p>Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/sep/18/arsenals-ethan-nwaneri-becomes-youngest-premier-league-player-at-15">youngest player to appear in the Premier League</a>, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/30/max-dowman-journey-billericay-to-history-with-arsenal">highly anticipated debut</a>. But after a week when Arsenal published <a href="https://www.arsenal.com/news/max-dowmans-incredible-list-of-records-for-club-and-country-azbFG5M3BWVo">an article</a> dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.</p><p>Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/kevin-de-bruyne-napoli-manchester-city-champions-league</link>
      <description><p>Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca</p><p>As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times.       <description><ul><li><p>‘Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible,’ says Villa manager</p></li><li><p>Turkish champions had to move game on Saturday</p></li></ul><p>Unai Emery has insisted he will not alter his plans for Aston Villa’s Champions League game at ­Galatasaray on Tuesday night on account of concerns about the state of the pitch. The Turkish champions hastily moved Saturday’s home fixture from Rams Park after starting emergency repairs to the surface this month. The Villa defender Ian Maatsen said he and his teammates were aware the pitch was in a “bad condition”.</p><p>Villa were informed by Uefa last week that they would be unable to train at the venue the day before the Champions League game in order to give the pitch maximum time to recover after heavy maintenance work.       <title>Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/timothy-weah-i-dont-want-to-beg-to-be-back-in-the-national-team</link>
      <description><p>Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad</p><p>This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says.</p><p>Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/06/usa-belgium-world-cup-2026-match-report">at the hands of Belgium in the last 16</a>. “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/timothy-weah-i-dont-want-to-beg-to-be-back-in-the-national-team">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/bayern-munich-jamal-musiala-controversy-bundesliga</link>
      <description><p>German giants’ treatment of midfielder has raised questions about how far the reputation of a family club still holds</p><p>It was, on paper, a perfect Friday evening for Bayern to flex their muscles once again, in the chill of their intimidating Allianz Arena against struggling opponents who had won just twice all season in the league. In the end, though, the best news of the night was that Saïd El Mala, the star of the visitors, Köln, who had scored a jaw-dropping consolation goal at the same stadium in spring, fluffed a far easier chance in the closing stages that would have condemned the champions to defeat.</p><p>The word crisis is rampantly overused in sport, but this was the weekend Bayern’s injury troubles reached critical mass. With Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismaël Saibari already missing, their talisman Harry Kane had his game curtailed after 20 minutes and by the time the second half had begun, they’d lost Michael Olise too.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/bayern-munich-jamal-musiala-controversy-bundesliga">Continue reading...</a></description>

This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/19/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">United’s victory at Anfield last season</a> was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.</p><p>Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">lost only 4-0</a>. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/mar/05/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023</a>. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/mauricio-pochettino-can-now-see-just-how-desperate-manchester-united-are">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/psg-best-attack-europe-desire-doue-acl-khvicha-kvaratskhelia-luis-enrique</link>
      <description><p>Désiré Doué sustained an ACL injury in PSG’s 3-2 win at Nice and joins Khvicha Kvaratskhelia on the treatment table</p><p>By <a href="https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/">Get French Football News</a></p><p>Luis Enrique is in uncharted territory, even if he insists that “it isn’t a first”.       <title>WSL talking points: captain Spence inspires Spurs’ shock win at City and Lionesses impress</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal</link>
      <description><p>We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place</p><p>Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">shock 3-1 victory</a> away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” <strong>Tom Garry</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report">Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/wsl-talking-points-tottenham-london-city-lionesses-chelsea-arsenal">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas</link>
      <description><p>Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change</p><p>“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, <em>this</em> was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ikiN2ah9DL4">Pelé against the Nazis</a>. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.</p><p>In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of <a href="https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37625798/sevilla-real-betis-laliga-best-rivalry-city-lives-sport">a city divided</a>, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled <em>the </em>game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

Son retour a provoqué un bond de 31 % de l’entreprise en Bourse.             <title><![CDATA[« Voir sa mère dans la pauvreté et être incapable de l'aider, c'est très dur », pourquoi ces pêcheurs veulent tous quitter le Sénégal]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[De jeunes pêcheurs de Yenne Todd, âgés de 18 à 22 ans, ne cachent ni leur désarroi ni leur envie de partir. Confrontés à des conditions de vie difficiles et à l'absence de perspectives économiques, ils disent ne plus entrevoir leur avenir au Sénégal. Alors que les vingt-et-un « trains de sanctions » édictés par l'Union européenne contre la Russie depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en Ukraine en février 2022 ont touché les hydrocarbures, le secteur financier ou les armements, Bruxelles vient de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa volonté de faire plier le Kremlin en s'en prenant au sport et à la culture, deux valeurs centrales de la société civile. Des propositions qui pourraient toutefois avoir du mal à se concrétiser du fait qu'elles puissent être considérées comme une attaque directe contre les citoyens russes...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4a1460cc-e7cb-11f1-87d4-9fbe8f526646</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:29:46 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg">© Reuters/Yves Herman </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit... le Bregret?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261123-dix-ans-apr%C3%A8s-le-r%C3%A9f%C3%A9rendum-sur-le-brexit-le-bregret</link><description>
Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit qui a présidé au départ effectif du Royaume-Uni de l’Europe... Londres opère lentement, mais sûrement un rapprochement avec le continent. Le Brexit a causé plus de mal que de bien, a résumé le nouveau Premier ministre travailliste Andy Burnham, qui n’exclut pas un retour de son pays dans l’UE. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">96183ba6-e762-11f1-a96c-7b5726cadb9b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 20:05:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Frédérique Lebel</dc:creator></item><item><category>La fabrique du monde</category><title>Pedro Sanchez peut-il réussir sa «remontada» et rester au pouvoir?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/la-fabrique-du-monde/20261123-pedro-sanchez-peut-il-r%C3%A9ussir-sa-remontada-et-rester-au-pouvoir</link><description>
Dernière ligne droite avant les élections législatives anticipées qui auront lieu ce dimanche 29 novembre en Espagne. Le scrutin s’annonce périlleux pour Pedro Sanchez, donné perdant dans les sondages. Spécialiste des « remontadas » spectaculaires, le chef du gouvernement socialiste pourra-t-il néanmoins faire mentir les sondages et rester aux affaires ?  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">14896756-e724-11f1-90c6-8324eea7e277</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:20:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Daniel Vallot</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: journée de grève nationale contre la vie chère, le trafic aérien entièrement paralysé</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-belgique-journ%C3%A9e-de-gr%C3%A8ve-nationale-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re-le-trafic-a%C3%A9rien-enti%C3%A8rement-paralys%C3%A9</link><description>
Il n'y aura pas d'avion dans le ciel belge ce lundi 23 novembre : c'est la conséquence d'une grève nationale contre la vie chère. Alors que le gouvernement fédéral belge cherche difficilement à négocier un budget de rigueur qui vise à économiser 10 milliards d'euros au cours des prochaines années, les syndicats ont appelé à faire front commun et à une « grande mobilisation citoyenne » pour dénoncer la politique d’austérité ainsi que la baisse du pouvoir d’achat. Une journée à laquelle ont décidé de se joindre les contrôleurs aériens, ce qui va entièrement paralyser le trafic des avions toute la journée. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b34cece-e719-11f1-9a3f-47fc1c531e42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:00:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg">© Mark Carlson / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Hongrie: la détention provisoire d'un ancien ministre d'Orban dans une enquête de corruption prolongée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-hongrie-la-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-d-un-ancien-ministre-d-orban-dans-une-enqu%C3%AAte-de-corruption-prolong%C3%A9e</link><description>
En Hongrie, Miklos Sesztak, l’ancien ministre du Développement national entre 2014 et 2018, et actuel député au Parlement hongrois, a été arrêté fin septembre. Il est soupçonné d’avoir détourné de l’argent public et d’avoir touché d’énormes pots-de-vin. Lors d’une perquisition à son domicile, la police a trouvé plusieurs coffres-forts vides. Il y a huit jours, les autorités hongroises découvraient un immense butin : près de 16 millions d’euros en liquide, cachés dans des forêts, des granges et des entrepôts. La détention provisoire de Miklos Sesztak a été prolongée jusqu’à fin janvier.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0120195e-e511-11f1-9083-078c74fc6df3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:36:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg">© AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Contre la guerre, pour la jeunesse: vague de manifestations à travers l'Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-contre-la-guerre-pour-la-jeunesse-vague-de-manifestations-%C3%A0-travers-l-europe</link><description>
Contre la « militarisation » de la société et la vie chère, pour l'avenir des jeunes, l'éducation, le droit au logement, le climat : des dizaines de milliers de manifestants se mobilisent à travers l'Europe vendredi 20 novembre, sur fond de rejet des institutions. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1853515c-e50e-11f1-8321-3bce4db5bc5f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:25:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg">© Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-le-danemark-va-expulser-un-diplomate-russe-apr%C3%A8s-la-tentative-d-assassinat-d-un-ukrainien-sur-son-sol</link><description>
Le Danemark va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie après la tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol, qu'il soupçonne Moscou d'avoir orchestré, a indiqué vendredi 20 novembre le ministre danois des Affaires étrangères. La diplomatie russe a promis de riposter. « Moscou donnera une réponse appropriée », a indiqué la porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Maria Zakharova, citée par l'agence de presse TASS.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7863937e-e507-11f1-99b0-bbfd8e7adaf9</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg">AFP - EMIL HELMS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Manifestations en Europe: «Une volonté de converger au niveau transnational et avec d'autres générations»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261120-manifestations-en-europe-une-volont%C3%A9-de-converger-au-niveau-transnational-et-avec-d-autres-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rations</link><description>
La mobilisation contre la vie chère traverse toute l'Europe : des millions de personnes sont attendues dans les rues contre la vie chère et pour le droit au logement. Ce mouvement de fond, lancé à partir de ce vendredi 20 novembre, traduit des réalités communes. Ces luttes peuvent-elles vraiment converger ? Quels modes d'action pour quelles revendications ? L’analyse du sociologue Paolo Stuppia, enseignant à Sciences Po Paris et co-auteur de Géopolitique de la jeunesse – Engagement et (dé)mobilisations, publiée aux éditions Cavalier bleu.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a69a8ac8-e4f2-11f1-a69d-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:07:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>À la Une: Aleksandar Čupić, le sage à la tête du Parlement serbe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-%C3%A0-la-une-aleksandar-%C4%8Dupi%C4%87-le-sage-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-du-parlement-serbe</link><description>
Une revue de presse des Balkans en partenariat avec Le Courrier des Balkans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb8a088e-e4f2-11f1-8ab1-dffd4ffb6f91</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:41:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Djordje Kojadinovic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>Courrier des Balkans</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>UE/Royaume-Uni: Andy Burnham annonce une «réflexion» en 2027 sur les relations à long terme</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-ue-royaume-uni-andy-burnham-annonce-une-r%C3%A9flexion-en-2027-sur-les-relations-%C3%A0-long-terme</link><description>
Pour son premier sommet avec l’UE, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham peut s’estimer satisfait. Européens et Britanniques se sont mis d’accord sur trois dossiers concernant les jeunes, les émissions de CO2 et les normes alimentaires. La « remise à zéro » imaginée par son prédécesseur Keir Starmer pour les relations entre Londres et Bruxelles est désormais sur des rails, même si union douanière, libre-circulation et marché unique restent des lignes rouges pour les Britanniques. Les Européens affirment avoir tourné la page du Brexit et se satisfont ouvertement des accords ponctuels comme ceux qui ont été trouvés ce vendredi 20 novembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f35856f6-e4f2-11f1-85c2-81e9611d4583</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg">AP Photo/Marius Burgelman - Marius Burgelman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Deux missiles russes tombent en Pologne, Varsovie dénonce «une provocation»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-deux-missiles-russes-tombent-en-pologne-varsovie-d%C3%A9nonce-une-provocation</link><description>
Des missiles russes sont tombés ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 en Pologne, non loin de la frontière ukrainienne, suscitant de vives réactions de Varsovie, de l'Otan, de l'Union européenne et du Royaume-Uni, tous alliés de Kiev. Le secrétaire général de l'Otan, Mark Rutte, se rendra à Varsovie samedi.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b07d5818-e4f2-11f1-be00-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:44 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ac76e586-e4f2-11f1-826c-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T091417Z-724863669-RC2KROAVQTVB-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-POLAND-OBJECTS.jpg">© Kacper Pempel / Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Decorre nesta segunda-feira a segunda edição da cimeira "Choose France" extrictamente reservada aos investidores franceses. No âmbito deste encontro organizado na cidade universitária internacional de Paris, são colocados hoje em destaque mais de 200 projectos industriais nacionais e cerca de 15 mil milhões de Euros de novos investimentos de empresas francesas dentro do país.

O Presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron, confirmou esta segunda-feira ao Le Figaro que está a estudar a possibilidade de inscrever na Constituição francesa uma regra que obrigue o Estado a controlar as suas contas públicas e a seguir uma trajectória de equilíbrio orçamental. A medida seria baseada num plano de reforma de 2011 que nunca foi aplicado por falta de votação final. A concretização da proposta vai depender da evolução dos mercados financeiros e da situação orçamental em Janeiro, precisou Emmanuel Macron ao diário francês. Para conversarmos sobre o tema convidámos o economista Carlos Vinhas Pereira.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24d547de-e50c-11f1-826e-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T172454Z-1063186339-RC24ROA9WSS5-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-GERMANY-BRITAIN.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24d547de-e50c-11f1-826e-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T172454Z-1063186339-RC24ROA9WSS5-RTRMADP-3-UKRAINE-CRISIS-GERMANY-BRITAIN.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ef4b7da0-e749-11f1-ad20-31f4bf0fddc0</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:28:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Carina Branco</dc:creator></item><item><category>França</category><title>França: Emmanuel Macron quer inscrever «a regra de ouro» na Constituição</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/pt/fran%C3%A7a/20261123-fran%C3%A7a-emmanuel-macron-quer-inscrever-a-regra-de-ouro-na-constitui%C3%A7%C3%A3o</link><description>
